mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, which may lead to inflation and negative S&P 500 returns as the Fed might tighten policy.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops below 3.5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate increased demand in the housing market, which can boost related sectors and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests stronger economic output, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong GDP growth (GDPC1) and low unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth and UNRATE meet the trigger but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 5% indicates inflation, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as the Fed tightens policy.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS declines but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real disposable income (RSAFS) may lead to reduced consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth is negative but S&P 500 returns are positive.
